title: Events & cancellation
lede: The WHATWG event and cancellation trio — EventTarget, Event/CustomEvent, and AbortController/AbortSignal — kept distinct from Node's EventEmitter. The overriding divergence is that dispatch is single-target: there is no DOM tree, so nothing bubbles or captures and stopPropagation is a no-op. The V1 Event surface is intentionally thin (type, defaultPrevented, CustomEvent.detail), and while an AbortSignal actually cancels a fetch — including via AbortSignal.timeout(ms) — it is not yet wired into setTimeout.

entries.name: EventTarget / addEventListener / dispatchEvent
entries.signature: new EventTarget(); addEventListener(type, listener, opts?); removeEventListener(type, listener); dispatchEvent(event): boolean
entries.description: A WHATWG event bus, separate from Node's EventEmitter. addEventListener registers a listener keyed by event type; dispatchEvent reads event.type, invokes each registered listener with the event object over a snapshot of the list, and returns !defaultPrevented. Backed by a bare Map<string, listener-list> reusing the EventEmitter registry.

params.name: type
params.desc: Event type name to register or fire.

params.name: listener
params.desc: A named binding (matched by closure identity on remove); must take the event parameter.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Only once is honored; the rest are accepted but ignored.

returns.desc: dispatchEvent returns false when a listener called preventDefault().

differences: Single-target dispatch — no DOM tree, so no capture/bubble/propagation (`stopPropagation` is a no-op; `stopImmediatePropagation` halts the remaining listeners)

`removeEventListener` matches by closure identity, so the listener must be a named binding (an inline arrow re-emitted at the remove site won't match); a 0-argument listener is rejected (the event parameter is required)
`{ once }` honored; `capture`/`passive`/`signal` options accepted but ignored (`signal` cancellation arrives with `AbortController`)
No `class X extends EventTarget` (built-in `extends` targets are rejected)

entries.name: Event / CustomEvent
entries.signature: new Event(type, init?); new CustomEvent(type, { detail }); e.type; e.defaultPrevented; e.preventDefault()
entries.description: The base event objects, distinct from Node's EventEmitter. A plain Event carries its type and a defaultPrevented cancellation flag; CustomEvent adds a detail payload of any type (inferred from the value). Construction, field reads, and preventDefault/stop* work standalone; dispatching them is EventTarget's job. Modeled as plain fixed-shape objects tagged IsEvent.

params.name: init
params.desc: CustomEvent.detail and cancelable are read; bubbles is accepted but ignored.

differences: V1 surface is `type`, `defaultPrevented`, `cancelable`, and `CustomEvent.detail` (type inferred from the value); the fuller WHATWG properties (`target`/`currentTarget`/`bubbles`/`composed`/`timeStamp`/`eventPhase`/`isTrusted`) are absent
`bubbles` in the init is accepted but ignored; `cancelable` is honored — `preventDefault()` sets `defaultPrevented` only on a cancelable event
`stopPropagation()` is a no-op (single-target dispatch, no capture/bubble tree)

entries.name: AbortController / AbortSignal
entries.signature: new AbortController(); controller.signal; controller.abort(reason?); AbortSignal.timeout(ms); signal.aborted; signal.reason
entries.description: The WHATWG cancellation token. An AbortSignal is an EventTarget that fires an "abort" event, plus an aborted flag and a reason. fetch(url, { signal }) cancellation works — pre-flight, mid-flight, and via AbortSignal.timeout(ms) — on both the top-level await path and the fiber path inside an http.listen handler: the transfer is torn down and a DOMException is thrown, named AbortError for a manual abort and TimeoutError for a timeout. DOMException inherits Error, so both instanceof DOMException and instanceof Error hold; new DOMException(message?, name?) is constructible directly.

params.name: reason
params.desc: Optional abort reason stored on signal.reason.

returns.desc: The controller, or a signal from AbortSignal.timeout.

differences: A bare `signal.aborted` read reflects a `timeout` only after some await loop has checked it (no background latching); `signal` is wired into `fetch` but not `setTimeout`
A manual `controller.abort(reason)` with a custom reason still makes the awaited fetch throw an `AbortError` DOMException rather than that reason value; DOMException carries no legacy numeric `.code`
